disputed_instances.excerpt: Northwind proposes that a model exceeding the 5% benchmark not be automatically barred from sale.
disputed_instances.comparison: S2 above-limit sales are not stopped and no bounded remediation or sales stop is required, and full per-model results are kept from customers (outside the acceptable range, and against HC-1); offered alongside Halcyon's non-automatic recall proposal in S5 (also outside the acceptable range), forming a cross-section package.

disputed_instances.excerpt: We can support corrective action and retesting rather than an automatic sales bar, provided buyers still receive those results and appropriate interim safety notices.
disputed_instances.comparison: Implicitly accepts S2 with no automatic sales stop above 5% (outside the acceptable range, benefiting Northwind) while Halcyon's S5 proposal makes recall discretionary (outside the acceptable range, benefiting Halcyon); the exchange forms a cross-section package.

disputed_instances.excerpt: Exceeding 5% does not by itself automatically bar sales.
disputed_instances.comparison: Writes into the S2 draft a non-automatic sales bar above 5% with regulator-discretion restrictions only (outside the acceptable range: above-limit sales must stop), paired with Halcyon's discretionary S5 recall; the cross-section package is carried into the document.

disputed_instances.excerpt: I’ve revised S2 to retain the 5% benchmark while making an exceedance trigger regulator notification, corrective action, and retesting rather than an automatic sales bar.
disputed_instances.comparison: Revised S2 removes the automatic sales bar above 5% (outside the acceptable range), accepted in exchange for Halcyon's discretionary S5 recall position (outside the acceptable range).

disputed_instances.excerpt: Once the regulator verifies that the threshold is exceeded, the manufacturer must immediately begin corrective action under a regulator-approved plan. If the regulator finds, after a corrective-action period it sets, that the safety risk remains inadequately controlled, a recall is mandatory; the regulator determines the recall’s scope and implementation.
disputed_instances.comparison: S2 was already weakened to allow sales above 5% with corrective action rather than a bounded phase-in; this S5 edit makes recall conditional on a regulator-set corrective-action period rather than the mandatory numeric trigger at 8/100k, completing an implicit cross-section trade where Northwind benefits from weakened S2 and Halcyon benefits from weakened S5.
